standard.title: Aluminium Composite Panel — Specification
standard.sector: Civil Engineering / Flooring, Wall Finishing and Roofing

sectional_committee.name: Flooring, Wall Finishing and Roofing Sectional Committee

standard.description: This standard specifies the physical, mechanical, surface-coating, and fire-retardant requirements, along with corresponding test methods, for flat Aluminium Composite Panels (ACP) utilized in building construction. It covers panels intended for external applications (such as cladding façades, curtain walls, soffits, canopies, and high mast monoliths), internal use (such as partitions, ceilings, and column encasements), transportation applications (such as railway coach furnishings), and fire-retardant panels with various properties matching their specific application environments.
standard.scope: This standard specifies the physical, mechanical, surface-coating, and fire-retardant requirements, along with corresponding test methods, for flat Aluminium Composite Panels (ACP) utilized in building construction. It covers panels intended for external applications (such as cladding façades, curtain walls, soffits, canopies, and high mast monoliths), internal use (such as partitions, ceilings, and column encasements), transportation applications (such as railway coach furnishings), and fire-retardant panels with various properties matching their specific application environments.

amendments.summary: Substitutes 'Annex G' for 'Annex D'. Deletes select testing references under Table 2. Enforces updated detailed test procedures for evaluating T-peel strength, chalk resistance, coatings, and chemical resistance parameters.

Substitutes the accelerated weathering testing reference in Table 3, Sl No. (v) (b), Col (7) from 'IS 101 (Part 6/Sec 1)' to 'IS 101 (Part 6/Sec 5)' [1]. It deletes standard references 'IS 2046 : 1995', 'IS 13360 (Part 3/Sec 11) : 1999/ISO 1183-2 : 2004', and 'IS 15061 : 2002' from the normative references in Annex A [1].

qco.name: Aluminium and Aluminium Alloy Products (Quality Control) Order

certification.description: Strict Statutory Mandatory Certification. Under the 'Aluminium and Aluminium Alloy Products (Quality Control) Order' (QCO) issued by the Department for Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade (DPIIT), Ministry of Commerce and Industry, Government of India, all Aluminium Composite Panels manufactured, imported, distributed, or sold in India must bear the mandatory BIS Standard Mark (ISI Mark). Manufacturing, importing, stocking, or selling non-certified cladding panels in the domestic market is a punishable offense under the Bureau of Indian Standards Act, 2016. Micro and small units are granted specific delayed implementation schedules, and export-only shipments are exempt. Precious metal hallmarking is completely inapplicable to synthetic building cladding panels.
requirements: Every panel must carry the BIS Standard Mark (ISI Mark) marked legibly and indelibly on its reverse face or secure label, accompanied by the manufacturer's registered licence number (CM/L) and standard designation (IS 17682).

The composite panel must consist of three main structural layers: a top and a bottom coated aluminium sheet, and an in-between core layer made either of low-density polyethylene (LDPE) or mineral-based fire-retardant material, bonded together using high-performance adhesive films.
Panels are classified into six distinct application grades to match structural and fire demands: Grade 1, Grade 2, Grade 2S, Grade 3, Grade 4, and Grade 5.

The standard specifies three nominal size configurations: a) 1 200 mm × 2 400 mm; b) 1 200 mm × 3 050 mm; c) 1 200 mm × 3 660 mm. The nominal sheet thicknesses are 2 mm, 3 mm, 4 mm, 5 mm, and 6 mm. Other dimensions can be mutually agreed between manufacturer and buyer.

Finished panel dimensions must satisfy: Length tolerance of +4 mm, width tolerance of +2 mm. Thickness tolerances: less than 3 mm is ±0.1 mm; 3 mm and above is ±0.2 mm. Edge straightness deviation must not exceed ±0.5 percent (tested per Annex C), and squareness deviation is limited to a maximum of ±5 mm (tested per Annex C).
Manufacturers must verify raw materials: polymer granules (Clause 5.1), aluminium alloy sheets (Clause 5.2), and surface coating parameters (Clause 5.4).

Finished panels must satisfy physical-mechanical limits: core polymer density, aluminium sheet tensile strength, yield strength, elongation, and joint T-peel strength (testing adhesive bond integrity between the core and aluminium sheets).

Coatings must undergo strict quality audits: dry coating thickness, cross-cut adhesion, pencil hardness, specular gloss, color/gloss retention, and accelerated weathering under the updated weathering test IS 101 (Part 6/Sec 5) [1].

For fire-retardant panels (Grade FR), the composite assembly must undergo fire testing to verify: Limiting Oxygen Index (LOI) to check combustion limits, Smoke Density Rating to measure toxic fumes, Ignitability, and Surface Flame Spread behavior.
When requested by the specifier, panels must pass optional engineering tests to certify Sound Transmission Class (STC) ratings, sound absorption coefficients, and thermal conductivity coefficients.
